transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-18 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Malik (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Lina (Meridian Head of ML), Arun (Cloud Eng), Maya (PM), Evan (Security)

Summary: Quick Q2 health check focused on capacity headroom, expected peaks for an upcoming product launch, cost tradeoffs between hosted vs dedicated, and a short security checklist. Team agreed to run a 48-hour stress test and exchange detailed traffic histograms.

Topics: usage spike forecast, cost modeling, autoscaling policies, dedicated capacity vs hosted fallbacks, KV cache and prefix caching, quantization playbook, SOC2/SSO/KMS questions, pilot kickoff date, next steps.

Action items (read aloud): see metadata.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sofia: Hi everyone, thanks for joining this checkpoint. We wanted to sync on your peak plans for the new release and make sure capacity and cost are aligned.
[00:15] Lina: Yeah, thanks. We have a big marketing push planned for mid July, expecting a 3x peak over baseline for about 48 to 72 hours, most of it between 14:00-18:00 UTC.
[00:28] Maya: Sorry, to clarify, the 3x is on inference traffic, not backend API calls right?
[00:33] Lina: Correct, inference only. Primarily chat completions and a reranking batch we'll run during off-peak.
[00:39] Arun: Our current stack is hosted endpoints with a mix of g4 and g5 sized instances on cloud provider. We're seeing p95 at ~240ms on average, p99 around 480ms, but that's with small batch sizes.
[00:50] Malik: Got it. For Redwood we can route by priority. A couple options: keep hosted but enable burst capacity, or reserve Dedicated pools to guarantee throughput. There's also Private if you need VPC and KMS.
[01:05] Evan: Quick security note — we'll need SOC2 docs and confirmation on customer-managed KMS for the pilot. Also SSO via SAML is required.
[01:13] Priya: We can send our latest SOC 2 attestation and integration guide. SSO via SAML is supported; we do a SSO test during onboarding.
[01:20] Lina: Can you explain cost delta between hosted and reserved? We have a rough budget and want to know thresholds for reserved economics.
[01:28] Sofia: Sure. Ballpark: for your typical model mix, hosted might run you about $0.0025-0.0060 per token depending on model and memory, while Dedicated reserved pricing becomes attractive once you commit to sustained throughput — think >2M tokens/day for multi-week events. With reserved you get predictable unit cost and admission control to avoid noisy neighbors.
[01:47] Maya: Are those numbers net of caching? We do significant prefix reuse which should reduce token volume.
[01:52] Malik: Good call. Automatic KV/prefix caching can cut tokens by 20-55% depending on reuse. For reranking we also recommend endpoint-side caching for candidate lists. We can model with your histograms.
[02:06] Arun: We'll share a 30-day histogram. Right now 60% of calls are short (<128 tokens), 30% mid, 10% long. Peak tail is what hurts us.
[02:16] Malik: That distribution helps choose quantization profile and batch sizes. For short sequences continuous batching with a 15ms scheduling window often yields best latency/cost trade. But long sequences push memory and KV cache behavior.
[02:30] Lina: Can Dedicated handle preemptive autoscale for burst? We need headroom without overcommitting spend.
[02:36] Sofia: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling and burst pools. You can reserve baseline capacity and allow burst to hosted or spare capacity in other regions as fallback. Also rollouts can pin model versions so you don't get unexpected perf differences.
[02:49] Maya: Regarding rollbacks — if a new model causes p99 spikes, what's the failover path?
[02:54] Malik: We recommend canary rollout (5-10%), monitor p95/p99, and automatic fallback to previous version if latency or error budget is exceeded. You can also route high-priority traffic to the reserved lane.
[03:06] Evan: About encryption — is KV cache encrypted at rest? Where are logs stored?
[03:12] Priya: KV caches on Dedicated are encrypted; logs can be retained per account policy. For Private deployments you manage KMS and audit logs stay in your cloud.
[03:22] Lina: For the 48h peak, I'm worried about warmup costs. How do we avoid paying for idle reserved GPUs when we're not at peak?
[03:30] Sofia: Two strategies: scheduled autoscaling and short-term reserved bursts. You can schedule increased min capacity for the 48h window. Or use Dedicated baseline + hosted fallback and only scale baseline for the window. We can run a cost model with your expected token counts.
[03:45] Arun: Can we get an example cost model for the 3x scenario — show hosted only vs reserved baseline + burst?
[03:52] Sofia: Yes, we'll send a runbook with a side-by-side. We'll include assumptions: token mix, caching benefit, batching efficiency, and quantization savings.
[04:02] Malik: One more technical—quantization: if you go 8-bit or 4-bit there's memory and latency tradeoffs. For short tokens 8-bit often gives best latency with modest quality losses; 4-bit is great for throughput but sometimes hurts p99. We can recommend model-specific quant profiles after benchmarks.
[04:20] Lina: Do you support on-the-fly quant switching? Like keep some versions quantized for burst?
[04:25] Malik: We have model variants. You can route surge traffic to a cheaper quantized variant if quality tolerates it. Also fallback routing will keep high-quality model for premium users.
[04:35] Maya: About observability, we want token-level cost breakdown and tracing hooks.
[04:40] Priya: Console shows token cost per route, latency histograms, and you can attach tracing IDs to correlate requests. We'll demo the dashboard in the pilot onboarding.
[04:50] Arun: For the stress test, what do you need from us?
[04:54] Malik: Ideally the same traffic pattern you expect (histogram + request shapes). We'll deploy a dedicated pool with your model and run generated load to confirm p95/p99 and error budget. We'll also test KV cache effectiveness by replaying prefixes.
[05:07] Lina: We'll anonymize payloads but keep token shapes.
[05:10] Evan: Security: can we run the stress test within our VPC with Private? We prefer not to ship logs out.
[05:16] Sofia: For the initial stress test we can run on Dedicated within Redwood's environment; for Private we can run the same steps once deployed to your VPC. If you need logs contained, we can redact or use ephemeral upload tokens.
[05:29] Arun: Ok. One more question on throttling — can we set per-API-key quotas and soft-limits to avoid cascading failures?
[05:35] Priya: Yes, we support rate-limits, per-key quotas, and can set traffic shaping policies. We also offer circuit breakers on error rates to mitigate cascades.
[05:44] Maya: I want the pilot timeline. If we aim for late June kickoff, what's the path?
[05:50] Sofia: Proposed: this week (6/18) exchange histograms and SOC2/SAML checklist. Next (6/21) Redwood sends pricing and pilot plan. Week of 6/28 - pilot setup and smoke tests. 7/5 - run 48h stress test. Then evaluate and decide reserved commitment.
[06:06] Lina: That timeline works if we can get the pricing and the SOC2.
[06:10] Evan: On SOC2, we'll need a short questionnaire about data retention and log access; expect follow-ups.
[06:17] Priya: Noted, Evan. We'll include a short FAQ with the attestation and retention options.
[06:23] Malik: I'll take point on the stress test and will ask for a few sample requests and the histogram. Anything special about reranking batch size?
[06:30] Arun: Our rerank runs with 32 candidates, about 1k batch jobs per day, usually scheduled between 02:00-06:00 UTC. The rerank is latency-insensitive but cost-sensitive.
[06:41] Malik: For rerank, we can batch more aggressively and use quantized variant to cut cost. We'll model that separately.
[06:47] Maya: On billing, how granular is the reserved billing period? Monthly? Can we do a one-off short commitment for the 48h?
[06:54] Sofia: We do monthly reserved commitments but also offer short-term burst credits and scheduled scaling. For very short windows, burst + hosted fallback often wins. If you expect recurring peaks, reserved is better.
[07:06] Lina: We'll decide on that after we see the pilot numbers.
[07:09] Sofia: Great. Any other questions?
[07:13] Maya: One small thing — can we tag requests for product bucket to see feature adoption?
[07:17] Priya: Yes, tagging and per-route cost breakdown is supported.
[07:21] Evan: Also, what's Redwood's incident escalation if production issues during peak?
[07:26] Sofia: For customers with Reserved or Private we have 24/7 support and escalation path; for hosted tier support windows differ but critical incidents get priority. We'll include SLAs in the doc.
[07:40] Lina: Ok, recap: share pricing, SOC2/SAML/KMS docs, produce cost model for 3x peak (hosted vs reserved+burst), run 48h stress test, send histograms.
[07:52] Sofia: Correct. We'll follow up with explicit dates in email.
[07:58] Malik: I'll share the stress test plan and the perf benchmarks we ran last month for similar customers.
[08:05] Arun: I'll get the histograms and request shapes by 6/20.
[08:09] Maya: I'll coordinate product tagging with Priya.
[08:13] Evan: I'll compile the security questions and send by 6/22.
[08:18] Priya: Thanks everyone. We'll schedule the kickoff meeting once we have the histograms and pricing acceptance.
[08:25] Sofia: Thanks all — we'll follow up.
[08:29] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcript quality: occasional misattribution and short gaps. Some product names transcribed as "Redwood Dedicate" or "Redwood Ded" in places due to background noise.
